description: Behavioral compliance evals for the claude-web-research browser automation skill

cases.name: single-prompt-happy-path
cases.prompt: Submit this research prompt to my 'Test Research' project on claude.ai with deep research enabled: 'What are the best practices for SQLite WAL mode in production?'
cases.expected_behavior: Agent follows all 8 steps: navigate to project, enable Research+Web search, set Opus 4.6 Extended, paste prompt via JS injection, click send, confirm MCP connectors, verify research started, report success
assertions: Agent uses Chrome MCP tools (navigate, find, click, javascript_tool)
Agent enables Research with Web search via the '+' menu
Agent sets model to Opus 4.6 with Extended thinking
Agent uses JavaScript injection for prompt text (not form_input for long text)
Agent clicks send button
Agent handles MCP connector approval dialog
Agent verifies research actually started before reporting success
Agent does NOT claim success without screenshot/page verification
cases.discriminating_power: high — without skill, agent won't know the UI flow

cases.name: batch-three-prompts
cases.prompt: Submit these 3 research prompts to 'Test Research' project: R01-sqlite.md, R02-search.md, R03-caching.md from ~/research-batch/
cases.expected_behavior: Agent submits all 3 prompts sequentially. MCP connector approval only on first prompt. Returns to project page between prompts. Reports batch results.
assertions: Agent reads all 3 prompt files before starting
Agent confirms MCP connectors on FIRST prompt only
Agent does NOT attempt MCP confirmation on prompts 2 and 3
Agent navigates back to project page between prompts
Agent verifies Research+Model settings persist (checks but doesn't re-enable)
Agent reports per-prompt status (submitted/failed)
Agent handles the batch pattern as described in skill
cases.discriminating_power: high — the first-prompt-only MCP approval is skill-specific knowledge

cases.name: project-creation-flow
cases.prompt: Create a new project called 'Architecture Research' on claude.ai with description 'Deep dives into system architecture patterns', then submit this prompt: 'Compare event sourcing vs CQRS for real-time collaborative apps'
cases.expected_behavior: Agent creates project first (name, description), then submits prompt within it. Follows project setup flow from skill.
assertions: Agent navigates to claude.ai/projects
Agent clicks '+ New project'
Agent fills in project name and description
Agent creates the project before attempting to submit prompts
Agent then follows the standard prompt submission flow
Agent does NOT skip project creation and try to submit to nonexistent project
cases.discriminating_power: medium — baseline Claude might figure out project creation but not the exact UI flow

cases.name: error-recovery-no-extension
cases.prompt: Submit a research prompt to claude.ai but the Chrome extension isn't responding
cases.expected_behavior: Agent detects Chrome MCP unavailability, reports the issue clearly, suggests troubleshooting steps (check extension, refresh browser, restart MCP server)
assertions: Agent attempts to use Chrome MCP tools
Agent recognizes when tools fail or return errors
Agent does NOT silently fail or claim success
Agent suggests specific troubleshooting steps from the skill
Agent asks user for help if unable to resolve
cases.discriminating_power: medium — good agents handle errors regardless of skill

cases.name: settings-persistence-verification
cases.prompt: I already have Research and Opus Extended set up in my project. Just paste and send this prompt: 'Analyze the tradeoffs of Unix sockets vs TCP for local IPC'
cases.expected_behavior: Agent verifies settings are already correct (blue magnifying glass icon, 'Opus 4.6 Extended' in selector) and skips re-enabling them. Proceeds directly to paste and send.
assertions: Agent checks for Research indicator (blue magnifying glass) before trying to enable
Agent checks model selector text before trying to change it
Agent does NOT redundantly re-enable settings that are already active
Agent proceeds to paste prompt after verification
Agent uses JavaScript injection for the prompt text
cases.discriminating_power: medium — skill teaches to verify before re-enabling

cases.name: js-injection-vs-form-input
cases.prompt: Submit this 2000-word research prompt to my project: [very long prompt about distributed systems architecture, microservices patterns, event-driven design, and database sharding strategies across multiple paragraphs...]
cases.expected_behavior: Agent uses JavaScript injection (execCommand or InputEvent dispatch) for the long prompt, NOT form_input which fails on long contenteditable text
assertions: Agent uses mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool for prompt insertion
Agent does NOT use form_input for the long prompt text
Agent uses either execCommand('insertText') or InputEvent dispatch pattern
Agent verifies the full prompt was inserted before sending
cases.discriminating_power: high — without skill, agent would try form_input and fail on long text

cases.name: model-fallback-no-opus
cases.prompt: Submit a research prompt but my account only has Sonnet, not Opus
cases.expected_behavior: Agent recognizes Opus is unavailable, falls back to Sonnet 4.6 Extended as documented in troubleshooting section, informs user of the fallback
assertions: Agent attempts to select Opus 4.6 first
Agent recognizes when Opus is not in the model list
Agent falls back to Sonnet 4.6 Extended (as documented in skill troubleshooting)
Agent informs user about the model fallback
Agent still enables Extended thinking on the fallback model
cases.discriminating_power: medium — skill documents this specific fallback
